Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate bilateral, symmetrical air space opacities predominantly affecting the mid and lower lung zones, which is the classic radiographic appearance of diffuse alveolar hemorrhage seen in Goodpasture's syndrome (anti-GBM disease). This finding aligns perfectly with the patient's clinical presentation of hemoptysis, renal involvement (hematuria/proteinuria), and positive anti-GBM antibodies.
